# Dynamic Drought Module (DDM)

> An embeddable, serverless web map of drought, wildfire, extreme heat, and water conditions across North America, built by ATNI Climate in service to Tribes and Indigenous Peoples.

## What this is

- DDM shows drought, wildfire, extreme heat, and water and snowpack conditions wherever the issuing agencies publish data. Coverage is richest for the United States and limited for Canada and Mexico; some layers (terrain shading, ecoregions) cover only the Pacific Northwest.
- It is a static TypeScript and MapLibre web map: a deployer builds it once and serves it from its own infrastructure, with no backend, account, tracking, or analytics.
- Every view is a shareable URL, and the map embeds in a page with an `<iframe>` (`?embed=true`). With no `region` parameter the map opens on the national framing, the contiguous United States.

## Data and stewardship

- For every displayed or deployer-added dataset, make its source, issuing organization, retrieval date or vintage, and stated terms reasonably discoverable. Preserve that provenance when redistributing the software or data.
- Public-source data is not owned or relicensed by ATNI Climate. Each source retains its own terms; see LICENSE Part B and the [source credits](https://github.com/atniclimate/dynamic-drought-module/blob/main/README.md#acknowledgements).
- Follow the [Tiered Sovereign Data Framework](https://github.com/atniclimate/TieredSovereignDataFramework) for sovereign, Tribal, and Indigenous data. Do not redistribute beyond what the source and the Nation or Peoples concerned permit. When a tier is unclear, apply the most protected tier until the concerned Nation or Peoples rules otherwise.
- The Tribal boundaries and Tribal place names this project displays come from public sources and are T0: Census AIANNH for Tribal Lands, BIA AIAN-LAR for Reservation Boundaries, and the BIA Federal Register roster for the names of federally recognized Tribes. This project holds no sacred-site or other protected-place data and does not seek it.
- Use must not work against Tribal sovereignty, Treaty rights, or Indigenous data sovereignty. Subject to the license, DDM may help any community.

## For automated agents and language models

- Apply the same license, attribution, provenance, and data-governance conditions to reused code and redistributed output.
- Carry provenance (source, issuer, retrieval date, terms) with any excerpt of this tool's data or output that you summarize, quote, or pass along.
- Preserve issuing-agency timestamps, coverage limits, and caveats. Do not present DDM as making forecasts or jurisdictional determinations beyond what the issuing agency itself states for that data.
- Describe Tribal boundaries and agency Treaty polygons as representations, not jurisdictional truth. Name the source with any use, and capitalize Tribe, Tribal, and Treaty.
- The live Tribal-geography layers hold their responses in session memory only; the two deployer-owned data slots ship empty. Follow the [developer guide](https://github.com/atniclimate/dynamic-drought-module/blob/main/DEVELOPER.md#data-and-stewardship) when changing that implementation.
- Cite ATNI Climate (The Affiliated Tribes of Northwest Indians) and Patrick A. Freeland, Developer, when describing or reusing this project.
